rows.en:
One... two... three...
Once again, we started counting over from the beginning.{p}

"It's fourteen after all.
Maybe just hanging up a tear-off calendar like that wasn't enough."
"That's not true.
That'll do the trick."
Sanae flatly shot down what I'd said.{p}

"But there's still the way down, isn't there?"
Yoko looked happy.
After what had happened earlier, she wanted to keep that scared feeling going, even just a little longer.
You know how you want to look at scary things even though they scare you?
That's actually pretty fun, right?
When you're thinking 'I'm scared, I'm so scared,' you're secretly having kind of a good time.
It was that kind of feeling, I guess.
That's why I think Yoko was smiling.
I nodded.
That's right, there was still the way down.
We had no idea how many steps there'd be going down.{p}

So we started counting.
Full of anticipation.{p}
"Ten... eleven... twelve..................thirteen...☆"{p}

Oh my gosh, maybe the three of us had wished hard enough, because the staircase had become thirteen steps!
All three of us fell silent, afraid of whatever was supposed to happen next.
We held our breath, bracing for it.
But you know what? Nothing happened at all.
Time just went by.
The first one to break the tension was Yoko.
Staring at the wall of the landing, Yoko sank to the floor right where she was.
She was shaking all over; it looked like her legs had no strength left in them.
"What's wrong?
Yoko, are you okay?"
"Look at that..."
As she said it, Yoko pointed at the wall with a trembling finger.
Sanae and I nervously turned our eyes that way.
And there...{p}

There was just a wall.
There was nothing in particular worth noticing.
...Huh★
Wait a second!
There was nothing on the wall.
Then what about the mirror Yoko had been looking into earlier★
That was what Yoko was trying to tell us.
Because I had seen a figure reflected on that wall too.{p}

Only Sanae looked blank.
"There was a mirror here before, wasn't there★"
"Geez, Reiko, what are you talking about?
The staircase in the old school building with the mirror isn't this one."
She was right!
I'd heard that the mirror had a story behind it too, but it was on a different staircase, the one on the opposite side.{p}

"Eeeeeeeeeeek☆"
Yoko and I screamed at the same time and took off running.
Sanae was startled by us and ran too, swept along.
The three of us fled the old school building as fast as our legs could carry us.{p}

It was still light outside, and we could see a few students here and there.
Once the relief set in, exhaustion hit me all at once, and Yoko and I were both heaving for breath.
"Let's call it a day."
It seemed Sanae had somehow picked up on how Yoko and I were feeling.
That's right, at times like that you want to get home before dark.
The three of us split up at the school gate.{p}

Nothing in particular has happened to us since then, but it still bugs me a little.
What was that figure Yoko and I saw back then?
Yoko even thought it was a mirror, so I think it was a girl about our age.
Hey, {c}{f:|}, what do you think it was?
A ghost?{p}Or maybe...?
I think it was a ghost
I think it was something else

Ahahaha, did that make you mad?
I know perfectly well you didn't mean it like that.{p}

Well, I don't really know what that thing was, but there was an interesting article in the paper a little while ago.
It was about a girl our age who died suddenly.
And the day she died was the very same day we snuck into the old school building.
The girl herself had nothing at all to do with this school, but, well, I think she was someone connected to Yoko.{p}

The paper ran a photo of the girl's face.
And her face looked exactly like Yoko's.{p}You get what that means, right?
Twin sisters
Just a chance resemblance

It's obvious, isn't it?
Yoko had a twin little sister who was adopted out to a relative's family when they were small.
Apparently Yoko wasn't very healthy when she was little.
So it seems that's why she and her sister ended up living apart.
The two of them knew about each other, and it seems they kept in touch a lot.
Though it seems they hardly ever got to meet...{p}

I think the figure we saw on the wall of the old school building that day was her sister's spirit body.
Maybe the spiritual energy of the thirteen steps made her sister's spirit body appear.
I told you her sister died suddenly, right?
Nobody really knows the cause of death.
Apparently she was in the middle of club activities when she suddenly lost consciousness and collapsed.
And she never opened her eyes again.{p}

Haven't you ever heard of out-of-body experiences?
Most of the stories are about people who are asleep.
You feel like you're floating in the air, and when you happen to look down, you see your own body sleeping.
I bet it was something like that.
Whether it's a spirit body or an astral body, if it can't get back into its own body... I mean its flesh, you die.
I think Yoko's sister couldn't get back into her own body, and she died.
Which means the three of us who went to the old school building killed her, right?
I do feel responsible, but nobody anywhere would ever believe something like this.
And Yoko, who I thought would be the saddest of all, doesn't seem to care much.{p}

Though sometimes she talks to mirrors and glass windows.
I wonder what that means.
Is Yoko seeing hallucinations from the shock?
Or is her sister staying by her side now?
Oh well, whatever.
It doesn't look like anything's going to happen from here on.{p}

But you know, {c}{f:|}.
From now on, be careful when you go on dates in the old school building.
That tear-off calendar is still hanging on that staircase.
Whatever happens, don't blame me.
Hee hee hee, that's the end of my story.
Come on, let's hurry on to the next one.{p}

How come?
I think the air's a little different in there.
...Oh well.
So anyway, we snuck over to that staircase so the teachers wouldn't catch us.{p}

Why are you so quiet?
{f:That ticks me off|Ugh, come on}!
You thought we were weird, didn't you?
I won't forgive that!
Whatever you think, {c}{f:|}, we checked the way down, too.
You can't know for sure unless you check both ways, right?
Hmph!
We checked the number of steps going down, too.{p}

...Huh?
That's weird.
Don't you hear a voice or something?
...What? No, no.
It's not me.
The babies never caught me.{p}

What?
You went by that staircase, but you didn't count the steps?
...Maybe you counted them without realizing it.
The human brain, you know, collects all kinds of information without you even being aware of it.
Like that you got into a fight with a friend yesterday, or that your homeroom teacher was wearing red...
There are things you remember even when you weren't trying to memorize them, right?
That's the power of the unconscious.
I bet you were counting the steps without realizing it, {c}{f:|}.
And maybe that's why this baby latched onto you, {c}{f:|}...{p}

Eww, {c}{f:|}, {f:stay away from me|don't come over here}.
I can't see the baby anymore, but isn't it riding on your shoulder or something, {c}{f:|}?
I kind of get that feeling.
{f:Go away|Sorry, but please don't come near me}.
{c}{f:|}, maybe you're the type who gets possessed by spirits easily?
You'd better be a little careful.
Come on, I said {f:go away|don't come near me}!{p}

...Not that there's any point in saying that, huh.
This club room is pretty cramped, after all.
.........
Well then, I guess we'll hear the next story.
Who's going to tell us the next one...?{p}
...That's the end of my story, but earlier, {c}{f:|}, you thought we were weird, didn't you?{p}

"I see...
So you can tell after all."
Fukuzawa murmured, and a slightly lonely look came into her eyes.
"Then I'll tell you a little about that ghost."
Did Fukuzawa know something about that ghost, {f:I wondered|I wondered}?
"This was a long, long time ago, back when the old school building was still in use.
There was a girl who killed herself because she was being bullied.
Nobody would have anything to do with her, and it hurt so much to have her very existence ignored that she hanged herself at that staircase...
She thought that if she did, everyone would surely look at her.
But not a single person cried for her.
Everyone forgot about her right away."
Fukuzawa was speaking slowly, as if choosing her words.
Her voice wasn't loud, but in the hushed room it had a strange weight to it.
"And so, the girl who died couldn't leave that staircase.
But nobody would look at her, just like when she was alive...
So she was lonely..."{p}

Huh★
What {f:was that|was that}?
It felt like something just passed through my head...
The old school building, a staircase, a crying girl...{p}

"Hey, {c}{f:|}.
You said you'd been to the old school building, right?
Did you meet anyone while you were there?
Try really hard to remember."
...Um, when was that{f:, now|, again}?
{f:I|I} went to the old school building with someone{f:|, didn't I}.
...{f:No|No}, {f:wait|that's not right}.
Maybe I went alone.
{f:That's weird|How strange}, I can't remember clearly.
"You walked down the first-floor hallway, didn't you?
Wasn't the floor creaking?"{p}

Oh, it was a {f:girl|girl}☆
I met a girl at the bottom of the stairs!{p}

"A girl..."
"Yes, just as I thought.
Do you know who she was?"
"No, I don't know that much...
But she was wearing this school's uniform, so I figured she was one of our students and {f:said|said} hello."
"So you spoke to her first."{p}

As she said it, Fukuzawa looked at {f:me|me} with a smile that sent a chill through me.
She was clearly different from the way she'd been until a moment ago.{p}

"Hee hee hee, sorry.
I was lying to you.
The story about the thirteen steps in the old school building was a lie.
I don't have any friends who'd go around with me."
"But why★
Was the whole story a lie{f:, then|, then}?"
"Not all of it.
The story about the girl who killed herself is true.
Because that girl is me!"{p}

Fukuzawa's face was turning into the face of a hideous mummy.
A tattered rope was coiled around her neck.{p}

"I've been so lonely, all this time.
I was all alone until you spoke to me that time.
I was even starting to forget my own name. But it's all right now.
I'm not lonely anymore.
Because now I have so many friends."
{f:What on earth|What on earth}...
A rope was wound tightly around {f:my|my} neck.
Not just {f:mine|mine}: every member in this room had a rope around their neck, and the other ends were gripped in Fukuzawa's hand.
Everyone was struggling desperately, but the ropes only dug in deeper...
My consciousness was slowly slipping away.
I couldn't feel my arms and legs anymore.
"I'm not lonely anymore."
Only Fukuzawa's voice was bright and bouncing.
The students who vanished from the club room...
{f:We|We} were going to become one of this school's seven wonders too............{p}

Well, they do say there are three people in the world who look just like you.
Hmm, I guess you could say that, but I see it a little differently.
I've heard of doppelgangers too, and usually it's your own double that you see.
They say if you see your own doppelganger you die soon after, but that isn't always the case.
The most famous one is probably the story about a European poet.
You see, back when he had no position or fame yet, he left his village, promising his sweetheart that he'd come back for her without fail.
At that moment, on the road in front of her house, he saw a fine young man on horseback coming from the opposite direction.
They say the rider was dressed in blue.
Then, a few years later.
The poet made it big in the city and went to fetch his sweetheart, just as he'd promised.
The road he'd once walked along, he was now riding back on horseback.
Thinking that, his heart skipped a beat.
Right now, he was wearing blue and riding a horse.
Just like the young man he'd passed long ago...
The one he'd seen back then had been his other self.
This poet went on to live for decades after that.
So seeing a doppelganger doesn't mean you'll die right away.
Though in this poet's case, you could also say time had crossed over.
So then, why do people say you'll die soon if you see your doppelganger...?
It's because a lot of people really do die, right?
And as for why they die...
Hmm, what I'm about to tell you is pretty far-fetched. Is that okay?
Then again, if I don't tell you this, the story won't end.
Oh well, if you can't believe it, just let it go in one ear and out the other.{p}

Do you believe in reincarnation and that sort of thing?
I do. Being reborn, I mean.
Most of the time, one life is reborn as one life, but they say once in a while a soul splits apart when it's reborn.
For example, let's say you and I, {c}{f:|}, were one single person in a past life.
Now the two of us have met here, so this state is what they call a doppelganger.
They say people who share the same soul look alike and give off a similar air.
That's why you end up thinking, 'There's another me.'
The reason it's tied to death is that the split soul tries to become one again.
And when that happens, the one who survives is usually the person holding the biggest fragment of the split soul.
Apparently sometimes they all die, though.
And even if they never meet, they say they can't live very long.
They're incomplete somehow, I guess.
Oh, and another example people give of a doppelganger is the astral body.
It means leaving your body, and I think it happens a lot to people who work themselves too hard.
When their body's already at its limit but they just can't take a rest... at times like that, the astral body alone slips out of the flesh and lies sleeping in their room, and so on.
Other people can see it too, so there are cases where you get a phone call from the person sleeping right in front of you, both of them really are that person, and everyone panics...
In that case too, they say most people die once they see their other self.{p}

...See? Pretty far-fetched, right?
I'm sure what Yoko saw was a doppelganger.
The spiritual energy of the thirteen steps must have drawn in a fragment of Yoko's split soul.
The girl who died and Yoko must have had different-sized pieces of soul.
Yoko hasn't noticed a thing, but ever since then she's been much healthier than before.{p}

They say neither one can live long as long as the soul stays split, so maybe it turned out for the best.
Hee hee hee, so how was my story?
Looks like your head's all jumbled up.
But I don't want to talk about it anymore.
I'm about to get confused myself.
Come on, let's hurry on to the next one.{p}

Hee hee, I knew it.
Mr. Miyama suddenly felt ashamed of how he'd been acting, too.
Once he calmed down and thought it over rationally, he regretted that ever since he'd confiscated the ring, he'd behaved in a way no adult ever should.
And what came back to him was the man he'd been when he'd had nothing but pure feelings for Ishikawa.
Why hadn't he treated her with the feelings he'd had back then?
He had taken the wrong attitude toward a girl in the middle of adolescence.
...He wasn't a bad teacher at heart, I guess.
The teacher decided this confession should be made to Ishikawa herself, so he took that ruby ring and headed for her house.{p}

Ishikawa was lying in bed.
Her haggard, pale face looked like Ogura's used to.
At first her expression hardened when she saw Mr. Miyama's face, but when he told her he'd come to give back the ring, she smiled happily.
The teacher confessed everything he'd done, apologized from the bottom of his heart, and finally added this:
"I'll wait for you as long as it takes, until your heart has settled."
And then he took the ruby ring out of his jacket pocket.{p}

(Huh, that's odd...)
Somehow the ruby in the ring looked darker.
(Was it this color before...?)
The teacher examined the ring, but it was definitely Ishikawa's ring.
It had Ishikawa's and Ogura's initials engraved on it.
(Must be my imagination...)
Thinking that, the teacher handed the ring to Ishikawa.{p}

Black smoke gushed out of the ring and wrapped around Ishikawa's body in an instant!
Ishikawa was coughing in agony, as if she couldn't breathe.
Mr. Miyama couldn't do a thing; all he could do was stand there dumbfounded and watch.
But the sound of her coughing went quiet in no time.
The black smoke slowly faded away, and there lay Ishikawa, her face twisted in anguish.{p}

She wasn't breathing anymore.
They say only the ring on her left hand was shining a beautiful red, just like it used to.
Ishikawa's cause of death was a heart attack, but there was nothing wrong with her heart.
Sure, she was sick, so maybe she'd gotten a little weak, but there was no way she should have had a heart attack.
All kinds of suspicion fell on Mr. Miyama too, but there was no proof of any of it, so he was never arrested.
But I bet the teacher knew what really killed Ishikawa.
What that black smoke gushing out of the ring really was.{p}

Wasn't it the curse the teacher had put on it?
He grumbled at the ring practically every night, remember?
That got packed into the ring as a curse.
And the curse was fulfilled, perfectly...
I think the teacher realized that, too.
After what happened, he quit the school and went off to shut himself away in the mountains somewhere.
Apparently nobody's heard from him since.
They say Ishikawa was buried with the ruby ring still on her finger.
Maybe she's up in the sky with Ogura now.{p}

Hee hee hee, you be careful too, {c}{f:|}.
Even if you don't mean to, there's no telling when or where you might be pouring a curse into something.
Did you trip over an empty can this morning?
Did you bang your head on the corner of a desk?
What did you think when that happened?
If you think anything too terrible...
...Well then, that's the end of my story.
Who are you picking next...?{p}

You'd set them free?
That's pretty cool-headed of you.
Yeah, living your whole life thinking only of someone who's dead is kind of sad, isn't it?
Precisely because they're precious to you, you want them to enjoy life for both of you, right?
Tying them to yourself when you don't belong in this world anymore is just selfishness, I think.
Well, I'm sure some people think that's love, and that's their call.
Ishikawa's a good example of that, isn't she?
'I've had the one love of my lifetime.
Ogura is my one and only eternal love...'
Only a truly pure person or a narcissist could think like that.
She's the self-infatuated type, isn't she?
Maybe all those incidents were really Ishikawa's own doing, and she'd just convinced herself it was Ogura's ghost...{p}

Hee hee hee, nobody can ever know the real truth, right?
That's where my story ends.
I'll tell you the thirteen-steps story some other time, so go and take a look for yourself once.
Then I'll tell you all about it.
Who's next...?{p}
